title: Care and replacement
moduleTitle: Shared: Job management and service delivery
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Inspect uniform, footwear and reusable protective clothing after each shift and document defects where required.
Separate clean and used clothing and manage contaminated laundry under workplace controls.
Request replacement items before clothing or footwear becomes unsafe and confirm a suitable replacement before the next hazardous task.

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Overview
instruction.body: This lesson develops practical competence in care and replacement for routine professional cleaning work. Apply the employer’s site procedures and stop if a task falls outside your training or authority.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body: Inspect garments and PPE, separate contaminated laundry, document defects and replace damaged items.

instruction.heading: Prepare and verify
instruction.body: Inspect uniform, footwear and reusable protective clothing after each shift. Identify tears, worn grip, stains, contamination and missing fasteners; clean items according to manufacturer and workplace instructions.

instruction.heading: Perform the work safely and professionally
instruction.body: Store clean and used clothing separately. Never take heavily contaminated protective clothing home if workplace procedures require controlled laundering or disposal.

instruction.heading: Check, record and escalate
instruction.body: Request replacements before clothing or footwear becomes unsafe. Document issued PPE and defects when required, and confirm a suitable replacement before the next hazardous task.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

qualityStandard: Uniform, footwear and reusable protective clothing are inspected after each shift.
Defects are documented where required, and damaged items are replaced.
Clean and used clothing are stored separately, and heavily contaminated protective clothing is not taken home where controlled laundering applies.
A suitable replacement is confirmed before the next hazardous task.
summary: Uniform, footwear and reusable protective clothing are inspected after each shift for tears, worn grip, stains, contamination and missing fasteners.
Clean and used clothing are stored separately, and contaminated laundry is managed under workplace controls.
Replacements are requested before clothing or footwear becomes unsafe, and a suitable replacement is confirmed before the next hazardous task.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do with a damaged piece of protective clothing?
options: Keep wearing the torn footwear until it fails and report it only if it breaks
Stop using the damaged item and request a replacement before the next hazardous task
Take contaminated protective clothing home to launder it and wash it with the family's clothes
Keep the worn item in use, since a minor tear is not a hazard and nobody will notice it

knowledgeChecks.question: How should a defect in issued protective clothing be handed over?
options: Document the defect and the issued PPE, and pass it to the supervisor
Put damaged PPE back in the clean store for the next person to use
Ask the client to fix it and then carry on with the job today
Keep the defect to yourself so the replacement is not delayed

knowledgeChecks.question: How should contaminated protective clothing be handled after a shift?
options: Keep clean and used clothing separate, using controlled laundering or disposal for heavy contamination
Store heavily contaminated protective clothing with clean uniforms in the same bag for the week
Take contaminated protective clothing home, to save the laundry trip and wash it with the family's clothes
Pack it with the next client's towels and send the bag to the laundry together with the towels

knowledgeChecks.question: Which practice with clothing and footwear is unsafe for a hazardous task?
options: Wearing footwear with worn grip for a hazardous task
Storing used clothing apart from clean clothing
Requesting a replacement before the grip wears out
Documenting issued PPE and defects

knowledgeChecks.question: What must be recorded about worn protective clothing before the next hazardous task?
options: Clothing defects need a record only after the job is finished and the record can wait until Friday
A verbal mention to the supervisor and the team leader on Friday afternoon at the end of the week
A record of issued PPE and defects, and confirmation of a suitable replacement before the next hazardous task
A photo in a personal chat sent to the supervisor and a friend and the whole team on the site
